synthesis: Scout users who forget their email or password after completing onboarding are permanently locked out. The current onboarding flow sends a ONE-TIME signed link that stops working once email_verified_at is set. Admins can 'resend onboarding' ONLY for unverified users (email_verified_at IS NULL), leaving no recovery path for verified users. The ticket proposes either (1) admin password reset OR (2) 'magic-link/passwordless like Clarity'. CRITICAL FINDING: Clarity does NOT use magic-links—it uses OTP (One-Time Password) authentication via email. The ticket's 'like Clarity' assumption is factually incorrect. Scout uses traditional email+password auth, while Clarity bypasses passwords entirely with OTP codes. No Laravel password reset infrastructure exists (no password_resets table, no PasswordBroker). The force-login mechanism referenced in ScoutUsersResource (line 346-354, route clarity-scout.force-login) is incomplete—ClarityScoutForceLoginController is imported in web.php but the controller file does not exist. Admin impersonation tokens exist (isScoutForceImpersonator checks in ClarityScoutAuthController) but are not fully wired.

acceptance_criteria.text: Scout user who forgets credentials can recover access without remembering original email/password (self-serve OR admin path must exist)
acceptance_criteria.notes: Ticket says 'self-serve without remembering email OR magic-link'. This is ambiguous—does it mean (a) self-serve that doesn't require remembering email, (b) admin-assisted magic-link, or (c) either approach is acceptable? The 'OR' likely means 'or use the magic-link approach' based on context.

acceptance_criteria.text: Admins can assist locked-out Scout users from the admin panel
acceptance_criteria.notes: Current 'resend onboarding' only works for unverified users. Need admin action that works for verified users too.

acceptance_criteria.notes: BLOCKER: ticket says 'magic-link/passwordless like Clarity (PREFERRED)' but Clarity uses OTP, not magic-links. Must clarify: (a) adopt OTP for Scout, (b) use signed URLs as 'magic-links', or (c) keep password auth + add recovery. 'Consistent with' is vague.

acceptance_criteria.text: No permanent lockout scenario exists without an admin recovery path
acceptance_criteria.notes: This is the core problem statement. After implementation, must verify no dead-end states remain.

questions.question: Should Scout adopt OTP authentication like Clarity (passwordless), or keep password auth and add password reset?
questions.notes: The ticket assumes 'magic-link/passwordless like Clarity' but Clarity uses OTP. If we align auth systems, Scout should move to OTP (no passwords at all). If we keep passwords, we need traditional forgot-password flow. This is a fundamental fork in the road.

questions.question: What does 'self-serve without remembering email' mean? Can user initiate recovery with phone, kit ID, or admin must look them up?
questions.notes: AC1 says 'self-serve without remembering email'—but how? Scout users are tied to kits. Options: (a) enter kit ID/GL number to look up email, (b) contact admin who looks up email and sends reset link, (c) support ticket flow. If truly self-serve, we need a non-email identifier.

questions.question: Should the existing signed onboarding URL mechanism be reused for password reset, or create a separate flow?
questions.notes: Current onboarding link is ONE-TIME (guardUser checks email_verified_at). Could (a) make it reusable by removing that check, (b) add separate scout.reset-password route, or (c) unify them with a 'purpose' parameter. Reusing means relaxing the one-time constraint, which has security implications.

questions.question: Should admins set a new password directly, or only generate a signed reset link that the user must click?
questions.notes: Security vs convenience trade-off. Direct admin password-set means admin knows the password (bad). Signed link means user sets their own password (better). But if user can't access email, signed link doesn't help.

questions.question: If Scout moves to OTP, does the PWA login form UI need redesign, or can it overlay OTP flow on password field?
questions.notes: Scout PWA is a separate Vue app. CustomLoginPage is Filament-only (Clarity admin). If Scout adopts OTP, ClarityScoutAuthController::login needs rewrite, and the PWA login UI needs corresponding changes.

questions.question: Should the partial force-login implementation be completed as part of this ticket, or is it unrelated?
questions.notes: ScoutUsersResource has a 'Login to Scout' action (line 346) that routes to clarity-scout.force-login, but ClarityScoutForceLoginController doesn't exist. prior force-login org-scoping work fixed org-scoped tokens for force-login, implying it was implemented then. May be dead code or incomplete. Relevant if admin-assisted recovery uses force-login pattern.

questions.question: What happens to pending signed onboarding links after a password reset? Should they be invalidated?
questions.notes: If a user has an unused onboarding link, then admin sends a password reset link, should the old link stop working? Laravel's signed URLs don't have revocation built in. May need to add a 'used_at' or 'invalidated_at' timestamp.

notes: prior onboarding signed-URL work precedent: Scout onboarding signed URLs use relative signatures (absolute: false) to avoid TLS proxy issues. Any new reset URLs should follow same pattern.
prior force-login org-scoping work precedent: Admin-assisted Scout login must stay org-scoped. Any force-login or admin-reset mechanism must respect org boundaries.
